template.name: Swipe cards — Decipher
template.description: Mobile-friendly full-image café swipe cards with native Decipher radio answers and accessible button/keyboard alternatives.
template.instructions: Use SwipeCards for a requested swipe-card single-select matrix. Supply label, title, instructions, and an array of rows with label/text/image. Keep column labels c1/c2/c3 and export values 1/2/3 fixed: Not interested/Not sure/Interested. Never turn Not sure into missing. After the last choice, preserve the bundled guarded completion through the actual native Continue button. Use one to twenty rows with unique valid Decipher labels. Use plain text only. Preserve native radio inputs and shared survey-level styles. Do not add shuffle, exclusive rows, open-ended cells, row conditions, or other interactive styles without a separate native verification. Put the rendered component in main, followed by a suspend. Generate no extra substantive questions for a single-question request. Within the component, keep the question, cards and Not interested/Not sure/Interested controls visible; the universal theme owns the surrounding shell. No review page, Back, Undo, card navigation, fallback toggle, debug display, progress labels or teaching copy. Disable native Back with ss:enableNavigation="0". Preserve accessible instructions. Hide native Continue only after successful enhancement; restore it and the matrix on validation/re-entry or after a stalled request. Finish the final animation, remove the deck, and invoke the existing native Continue button once when every row is selected. Never bypass native validation with form.submit or introduce repeated automatic retries. Each component is a plain native radio question. Keep exactly one pair of respview.client.css/js hooks at survey level, never copy styles into each question. Multiple instances may share a page or appear on separate pages; give each question a unique label. Automatically continue only after every enhanced question on a page is complete and no other visible question types are present. When mixed with other questions, leave Continue visible and let native validation handle the whole page. Keep the bundled pointer tracking, edge fade, directional cue, threshold snap-back, locked single-commit animation and subtle next-card preview; buttons use the same transition. Respect reduced motion and vertical scrolling. Verify native required validation and output mapping after generation. The base owns the universal Questra theme, including page shell and native controls. Preserve its early head CSS and bounded progressive enhancement gate; keep component behavior separate. Photo-card revision: each row must also supply image, the filename of a survey-owned static JPEG. Upload bundled public images before testing. Keep row text plain; image is rendered by the component-owned span and is decorative because the title and ingredients convey the concept. Preserve the gradient, responsive sizing and image-error fallback.

components.name: SwipeCards
components.description: Full-image mobile swipe cards with readable text overlay and native three-column radio answers.

label.description: Unique native question label, e.g. QSwipe. Use a letter followed by letters/digits/underscore.

instructions.description: Plain text respondent instructions. Not sure is an explicit answer.

rows.description: One to twenty unique rows in display order. Each label must be a valid unique native row label.

label.description: Unique native row label, e.g. r1.

text.description: Plain text card content; no markup, media, or logic.

image.description: Survey-owned static JPEG filename, e.g. honey-oat-latte.jpg. Use only a valid filename, no quotes or path traversal.
